assumptions: This pilot reuses one two-junction synthetic EPANET network; it is not a multi-topology corpus.
A declared additional junction demand is a deterministic synthetic withdrawal proxy, not a calibrated leak model, pipe-break model, or utility operating condition.
Each scenario is executed independently from the same frozen base input; the runner records first-period pressure at J1 and J2 only.
Scenario order and all perturbation values are frozen in this plan; no random sampling or hidden ground-truth leakage into the measurement features is used.
The pinned EPANET source revision is passed explicitly to the CLI and the executable binary is hashed.
nonclaims: No scenario is an actual municipal network or incident.
No calibration, sensor-noise model, pressure-dependent demand analysis, topology-generalization claim, cost model, or field performance is established.
These five runs are a plumbing pilot only; they are not the 1000-scenario, three-topology localization benchmark.
A simulated withdrawal is not evidence of a real leak or the cause of a pressure change.
No fieldwork, intervention, operational control, or automated actuation is authorized.
